verses.english: 2. Rolling Forth the Wheel of Dhamma
“Mendicants, I’ve declared: ‘This is the noble truth of suffering.’

verses.pali: Tattha aparimāṇā vaṇṇā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā saṅkāsanā:
verses.english: For that there are limitless arrangements, phrasings, and illustrations:
‘This is another way of saying that this is the noble truth of suffering.’
I’ve declared: ‘This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering.’ …
I’ve declared: ‘This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.’ …

verses.pali: ‘idaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccan’ti, bhikkhave, mayā paññattaṁ.
verses.english: I’ve declared: ‘This is the noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.’

verses.pali: Tattha aparimāṇā vaṇṇā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā saṅkāsanā:
verses.english: For that there are limitless arrangements, phrasings, and illustrations:
‘This is another way of saying that this is the noble truth of the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.’

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yogo karaṇīyo …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti.
verses.english: That’s why you should practice meditation …”
